description: Per-endpoint success words. input.body is the raw reply to input.endpoint with input.http_status, for a call that expects input.expect (object or list); expected as in not_ok_classification.json ({returns} or {error, emsg, message}). Success is a stat string compared exactly (no trimming, no normalising), except the GTT and OCO words, which compare ignoring letter case only (casefold on both sides; the test environment answers 'OI created'): PlaceGTTOrder 'Oi created', ModifyGTTOrder 'Oi replaced', CancelGTTOrder 'OI deleted' (the word the test environment answers; the documented 'Oi delete success' is no longer a success, it is OrderStatusUnknownError, owner decision 2026-11-18), PlaceOCOOrder 'OI created', ModifyOCOOrder 'OI replaced', CancelOCOOrder 'OI deleted' (each also needs a non-blank string al_id and no emsg other than a blank string), PlaceIceBergOrder, ModifyIceBergOrder and CancelIceBergOrder 'true' (the string, case-sensitive), every other endpoint 'Ok'. A stat 'Invalid Oi' (casefold, nothing trimmed) on ModifyGTTOrder, CancelGTTOrder, ModifyOCOOrder or CancelOCOOrder is a definite failure decided by the stat alone (with or without al_id, with an emsg, at any HTTP status): {error: OrderRejectedError, emsg: the stat text as received (so 'INVALID OI' stays upper case), message: 'Invalid Oi'} (the message is exactly that text, not the usual '<Endpoint> failed: ...' form); on PlaceOCOOrder and every other endpoint it is not a failure word. Not_Ok keeps the classification of not_ok_classification.json; on the three iceberg writes only, 'false' is a definite failure classified the same way, its message from a non-blank rejreason, else emsg. Any JSON array on the nine writes with their own words, whatever expect, and anything else on them is OrderStatusUnknownError; on a read it is a ResponseParseError.
